title: Steps to Super Cool Your Home
desc: Looking to take the steps to super cool your home during the hot summer months? Contact Rosenberg Indoor Comfort today to get started!

blocks.text: It seems like there is no end to the heatwave. How do you cool down your San Antonio house before the sun rises and cooks you all over again? While the best bet is to invest in a quality air conditioning system from Rosenberg Indoor Comfort, there are a few tricks you can use until the AC is installed.
Position an Exhaust Fan at Night

You know that warmer will get trapped near the ceiling, on the second floor, or in the attic. Over an extended period of time, it actually becomes a warming blanket for the whole house. Once the sun sets and the outside temperature starts to drop, place a box fan in an upstairs window facing out. Turn it on. Cool air will be drawn into the house from open windows downstairs or in the basement, bringing a breath of calm overnight. All that trapped hot air will be tossed outside.

If your home doesn’t have a large wrap around porch that keeps the direct sun off your windows, you need blackout curtains. Bright sunshine heats up old window glass and traps that heat inside your house. Placing blinds, insulated curtains, or even a dark sheet over your sun-side windows will stop that solar energy from heating up the house.

Not only does a well-insulated home keep the house warmer in the winter, it helps to block summer heat from entering your house. Adding an extra blanket of roll insulation in the attic is a start, but insulating the walls in older homes can reduce your energy bill by as much as 30%. It will block drafts, which are actually a superhighway for that sticky hot air to invade. For now, use spray foam and weather-stripping to block gaps around windows, doors, and even your foundation for a more comfortable home.
